The `Parser.createDefaultValueParser` method sets up a parser with default values for options. It creates a `Parser` instance, sets a help trigger, specifies options (such as the `b` option with a list of default values), and returns the configured parser.

The failing test `testSingleOptionSingleArgument` in `BugCLI158Test` sets up the parser with default values `["100", "1000"]`, specifies an argument of `"1"` for the `-b` option, and then asserts that the values retrieved for `-b` match the expectations.

The current bug report describes a behavior where defaults only work if no arguments are submitted. The expected behavior is for defaults to be picked up even when arguments are provided.

By looking at the implementation of the `Parser.parse` method, we can see that defaults are picked up using the `group.defaults(commandLine)` method. This suggests that the issue may be related to how defaults are processed or applied during parsing.

Next, I will look into the `group.defaults` method to understand how defaults are handled and identify any potential issues that could lead to the observed behavior.

The `OptionImpl.defaults` method in the Apache Commons CLI2 library is a no-op by default, meaning it does nothing to set default values on the command line for the specified option.

This finding explains why the defaults might not be working as expected in the test scenario for the `-b` option. Since the `OptionImpl.defaults` method does not handle setting default values, the behavior observed in the failing test where defaults only work if no arguments are submitted is expected.

To resolve the issue and make defaults work regardless of whether arguments are passed in, one possible solution would be to enhance the `OptionImpl.defaults` method to correctly set default values on the command line for the specified option.

The following methods need to be fixed:
- `org.apache.commons.cli2.option.OptionImpl.defaults(org.apache.commons.cli2.WriteableCommandLine)`

These methods should be modified to correctly set default values on the command line for their respective options, ensuring that defaults are applied even when arguments are provided.

By improving the handling of default values in the `OptionImpl.defaults` method, the expected behavior of picking up defaults regardless of arguments being submitted can be achieved.
